Subject: Nexa pilot: MAP + sequencing questions

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nexa is keen to move the pilot to a November start but procurement/legal have a few sequencing questions before we lock dates: 

1) We want clarity on whether the MSA or the DPA must be executed first for the pilot. Procurement prefers to have the MSA signed before anything else, but security has asked whether a DPA signature is a hard gating item for the pilot.

2) For acceptance criteria: do you require an order form to be signed for the pilot to be considered “accepted,” or can we run a short trial under a purchase order/statement of work?

3) Evidence pack: procurement asks whether a SOC 2 snapshot + vendor questionnaire is enough, or if you need additional artifacts (pen test, ISO certs).

4) Timeline: we’re targeting a pilot kickoff week of 11/10–11/14. If those dates are optimistic for Redwood’s legal ops, please advise the minimum lead time.

Can you put together a sequencing recommendation and a short mutual action plan (MAP) we can share internally? Procurement will need to confirm net payment terms and whether a pricing hold can be extended until signature.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — Kate

Hi Kate — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short sequencing recommendation and attached a MAP draft (Redwood_MAP_draft.xlsx) that lays out milestones, owners, and target windows. High-level answers below; MAP has the details.

Summary (short):
- Preferred sequencing: 1) MSA redline/review and signature, 2) DPA review concurrently but we aim to execute DPA at or right after MSA signature, 3) Order form finalization and signature (order form binds pricing and quantities), 4) Activation & pilot start.
- Acceptance: we can run a pilot under an order form (preferred) or a short-term purchase order with an SOW addendum — order form just speeds billing and activation.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II snapshot + completed vendor questionnaire is sufficient to start a pilot. If security requests pen test artifacts we can provide summaries; ISO/etc usually not required for pilots.
- Timeline: to get to an 11/10 kickoff for a pilot that includes legal review, we should: MSA redlines back within 5 business days, DPA review in parallel, order form signed within 3–5 business days after terms agreed. That is tight but achievable if procurement/legal commit to review SLAs in the MAP.

Key asks for Nexa:
- Confirm whether procurement will sign MSA first (your note suggested yes).
- Confirm acceptance window (how long you need post-pilot to accept).
- Confirm net payment terms preference and whether a pricing hold to 11/15 is needed.

I’ve CC'd Laura (legal) for clause-level notes and Chloe (CS) to confirm acceptance criteria language and activation sequencing. Laura — can you review the MAP draft and add any hard gating clauses (data residency, audit rights) that would block a pilot? Chloe — can you confirm the standard 14-day acceptance window or suggest changes?

Attachment: Redwood_MAP_draft.xlsx (MAP with milestone dates, owners, evidence list)

Thanks — Michael

Michael / Kate — quick legal read below and a recommended sequencing that reduces risk while keeping the 11/10 target in view. I attached a short evidence matrix (Nexa_evidence_matrix.pdf) that mirrors the MAP artifact list.

Legal comments (high level):
- MSA vs DPA: Redwood prefers the MSA to be negotiated and signed first (it contains many operational and liability clauses that govern the engagement). The DPA contains data processing specifics — we typically sign it concurrently or immediately after MSA (so that both legal frameworks are in place at activation). If Nexa insists, we will accept DPA before MSA for pilot-only limited-scope access, but we would prefer both executed before production traffic.
- Hard gating clauses to note: data residency (if Nexa requires EU-only), audit rights and subprocessor disclosure timeline. If Nexa needs a custom audit clause we will need 2–3 extra business days.
- Order form: binds quantities/pricing. For pilots we can accept a PO or an order form. If Nexa wants to delay order form until after pilot acceptance, include a signed PO plus written acceptance criteria as an SOW addendum.

Recommended sequencing (legal-friendly, minimal friction):
1) Day 0–2: Shared MAP + legal evidence request (SOC 2 snapshot, vendor questionnaire)
2) Day 2–7: MSA redline cycle (aim for redlines back in 3 business days; we will respond within 2 business days)
3) Day 2–9: DPA review in parallel (target execute on signature day of MSA)
4) Day 9–12: Order form finalization & signature (or signed PO + SOW if procurement needs that path)
5) Day 12–14: Activation & pilot kickoff window

Fallback: If MSA is delayed beyond Day 7, Redwood can issue a 30-day pilot addendum (limited scope, pre-approved minimal T&Cs) to unblock activation while legal finish full MSA/DPA. This avoids lost time on both sides.

Attachments: Nexa_evidence_matrix.pdf (requested evidence and expected delivery dates)

Happy to walk through any clause—happy to hop on a 20-min call if Kate wants a clause-by-clause.

Laura Bennett
